items.prompt:
1. Seeds of one variety were soaked in water for 0, 2, 4 or 8 hours, then kept at 25 °C, and the number that germinated after 5 days was recorded. Which is the independent variable?
A. Soaking time
B. Number of seeds germinated
C. Temperature
D. Seed variety

2. Which heading correctly records a mass measured in grams?
A. g / mass
B. Mass / g
C. Mass / cm³
D. Time / g

3. Which statement describes a systematic error?
A. Readings scatter either side of a value
B. A balance has the same zero offset each time
C. Two seedlings grow differently
D. An observer occasionally starts late

4. Which axis convention is appropriate?
A. Independent on y
B. Dependent on x
C. Independent on x
D. Both variables on one axis

5. What does a stopwatch measure in an endpoint trial?
A. Mass
B. Volume
C. Temperature
D. Elapsed time

6. What does a biological line drawing need?
A. Shaded texture
B. Parts that cannot be seen
C. Clear observed outlines
D. A remembered ideal shape

7. Which is an observation?
A. The sample is purple
B. The sample must contain a particular substance
C. The treatment caused the effect
D. The hypothesis is correct

8. Which precaution reduces parallax when reading a scale?
A. Read from one side
B. Read with the line of sight perpendicular to the scale
C. Use more decimal digits
D. Ignore scale divisions

9. A sample has 12 germinated seeds out of 20. What is its germination percentage?
A. 12 percent
B. 20 percent
C. 60 percent
D. 80 percent

10. A cube doubles in side length. What happens to its volume?
A. Doubles
B. Becomes fourfold
C. Becomes eightfold
D. Halves

11. Set P readings are 4, 10 and 16 mm; set Q readings are 9, 10 and 11 mm. Which statement is correct?
A. Set Q has the narrower spread
B. Set P has the narrower spread
C. Set P has the larger mean
D. Set Q must be more accurate

12. Which equals 0.25 mm?
A. 25 μm
B. 250 μm
C. 2500 μm
D. 0.25 μm
items.canonical_answer:
1: A. A differs between treatments; B is the dependent variable that was recorded; C and D were kept the same, so they are controlled variables.
2: B. B names quantity and unit; A reverses their order; C gives a volume unit; D mismatches quantity and unit.
3: B. B is a consistent bias; A and D describe variable scatter; C is biological variation.
4: C. C is the convention; A/B reverse it and D does not represent paired values.
5: D. D is the measured quantity; A needs a balance, B volume apparatus and C a thermometer.
6: C. C records what is seen; shading (A) does not belong in a line drawing, and B and D add detail that was not observed.
7: A. A is directly seen; B–D are deductions or causal conclusions.
8: B. B lines the eye up with the mark being read; A causes parallax, C adds unsupported precision and D loses the scale reference.
9: C. C follows 12/20 multiplied by 100; A/B repeat raw counts and D uses an unrelated value.
10: C. Volume scales with the cube of length; A uses a length factor, B an area factor and D reverses the change.
11: A. Set Q covers 2 mm and set P covers 12 mm. Both means are 10 mm, and a narrow spread shows consistency, not accuracy.
12: B. B converts using 1000 μm per mm; the other factors do not preserve the length.
marking_guidance: 1 mark for each question answered with the correct option (the key).
No mark for a distractor (any wrong option), or for more than one option chosen.
items.provenance: Original Codex activity; invented readings; proposed marking guidance.

(c) Calculate percentage germination after 2 h soaking. [2]
(d) Describe the observed relationship, quoting values. [2]
(e) Explain why the reported trend does not establish that soaking for 12 h would give 100 percent germination. [2]
items.canonical_answer: (a) Soaking duration. (b) Germination count or percentage at five days. (c) 26 ÷ 40 × 100 = 65 percent. (d) Germination rises from 40 percent without soaking to 80 percent after 4 h, over the tested range. (e) The supplied values cover 0–4 h rather than 12 h. The trend may plateau or reverse beyond that range, so 100 percent at 12 h is not established.
marking_guidance: (a) 1 mark: names the factor the learner changes, soaking time.
(b) 1 mark: names what is measured, the number or percentage of seeds germinated.
(c) 1 mark: shows the working, 26 out of 40 multiplied by 100.
1 mark: gives the answer, 65 percent.
(d) 1 mark: says that germination rises as soaking time increases.
1 mark: quotes values, such as 40 percent at 0 h and 80 percent at 4 h.
(e) two creditable points.
1 mark: says the data only cover 0 to 4 h, so 12 h was not tested.
1 mark: says a trend need not continue, so 100 percent is not established.

items.prompt:
A learner times water delivered through the same apparatus at three settings, using the same collected volume of 30 cm³ each time. These repeat times are recorded.

| Setting | Trial 1 / s | Trial 2 / s | Trial 3 / s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Low | 60 | 62 | 58 |
| Medium | 40 | 42 | 38 |
| High | 20 | 21 | 55 |

(a) Identify the independent and dependent variables. [2]
(b) Calculate the mean time at Low, showing working. [2]
(c) Describe the supported trend using the consistent readings. [2]
(d) State one controlled quantity specified by the method. [1]
(e) Identify the anomalous reading and say why it is anomalous. [1]
(f) The learner starts timing after some water has already entered the collector, with a different delay each trial. Identify the error and suggest an improvement. [2]
items.canonical_answer: (a) Chosen apparatus setting; elapsed time for 30 cm³. (b) 60 + 62 + 58 = 180 s; 180 ÷ 3 = 60 s. (c) From Low to Medium to High, the consistent times fall from about 60 to 40 to 20–21 s, indicating faster delivery for a fixed volume. (d) Collected volume, 30 cm³. (e) 55 s at High, because it is far from the other two readings, 20 s and 21 s. (f) An inconsistent late start under-records time by unequal amounts. Start timing at the same defined moment collection begins.
marking_guidance: (a) 1 mark: names the chosen setting as the independent variable.
1 mark: names the elapsed time as the dependent variable.
(b) 1 mark: shows the method, adding the three times and dividing by 3.
1 mark: gives the answer, 60 s.
(c) 1 mark: says the time falls from Low to Medium to High.
1 mark: quotes consistent data, about 60 s, 40 s and 20 s, which shows faster delivery of the fixed volume.
(d) 1 mark: names the controlled quantity, the 30 cm³ collected.
(e) 1 mark: identifies the 55 s reading at High as the anomaly because it is far from 20 s and 21 s.
(f) 1 mark: explains the effect of the error, that each time is too short by a different amount, so the trials cannot be compared.
1 mark: gives an improvement, starting the timing at the same defined moment each time.
